name: Reminders
description: Your reminders and lists as a projection of the personal vault: the open board, smart lists, projects and sections, and the trash. Calendar is its own app and shows a reminder on its day, read-only.

vault.why: Shows your reminders and lists, and lets you add, finish and organise them.

actions.name: link
phrasings: link the passport task to Sam
connect the dentist task to my trip note
link the rent task to Friday's event
actions.description: Link a task to any other item (a person, place, event, task, note, document, photo, account, transaction or workout) through edge.add (rel links, from the task); never to a Locker item. A link has no direction: it shows on both pages, and linking twice changes nothing.

actions.name: unlink
phrasings: unlink the passport task from Sam
disconnect the dentist task from my trip note
take the link off the rent task
actions.description: Take the link between a task and another item off through edge.remove (rel links, from either end); both items stay.

actions.name: add-task
phrasings: remind me to call the plumber tomorrow
add a task to buy milk
put 'file taxes' on my list for April 15
actions.description: Add a task through task.add: dated, prioritized, estimated, repeating, reminded, linked, filed in a project and section, or as a subtask of an open top-level task; or founded already done (`done_at`), which is how a completed imported item lands.

id.description: The id the shell minted for this write (#922 G2); omitted, the vault mints one.

due.description: A day, a wall clock or an instant.

rule.description: An RFC 5545 recurrence rule; the vault refuses one it cannot expand, and a repeating task needs a due date.

url.description: A link the task points at; null clears it.

done_at.description: Founds the task already done, at this instant: an import of a completed item.

actions.name: edit-task
phrasings: rename the plumber task
make buying milk high priority
add a note to the taxes task
actions.description: Edit a task's title, note, link, due date, priority, effort, reminder lead time or repeat rule through task.edit. A key that is present is set (null clears it); a key that is absent is left alone.

due.description: A day, a wall clock or an instant.

rule.description: An RFC 5545 recurrence rule; the vault refuses one it cannot expand, and a repeating task needs a due date.

url.description: A link the task points at; null clears it.

actions.name: complete-task
phrasings: mark call the plumber done
I finished the taxes
check off buy milk
actions.description: Complete a task through task.complete: the one completion operation Tasks, People and automations share. A repeating task gets its next occurrence, carrying its project, tags and what it is about; completing a completed task changes nothing.

actions.name: reopen-task
phrasings: reopen call the plumber
the taxes aren't done after all
uncheck buy milk
actions.description: Reopen a completed or cancelled task through task.reopen; it spawns nothing.

actions.name: cancel-task
phrasings: cancel the plumber task
I'm not buying milk anymore, drop it
cancel this week's repeat of the laundry task
actions.description: Cancel a task through task.cancel: it ends this occurrence with no successor (the Logbook's Won't do).

actions.name: organize-task
phrasings: put the plumber task in the Home project
file buy milk under Errands
move the taxes task to the Finance project
actions.description: File a task through task.organize: its project and section (null is the Inbox), its place in the list, and what a repeat counts from. Moving to another project leaves the section behind unless one is named.

actions.name: delete-task
phrasings: delete the plumber task
trash buy milk
remove the old taxes task
actions.description: Move a task and its subtasks to the 30-day trash through entity.trash; the Logbook keeps nothing.

actions.name: purge-task
phrasings: erase the plumber task forever
permanently delete the trashed milk task
purge the old taxes task
actions.description: Delete a trashed task and the subtasks trashed with it forever through entity.purge (#1015 D1); a subtask restored on its own is promoted to a top-level task first.

actions.name: empty-trash
phrasings: empty the task trash
clear out the trashed tasks for good
permanently delete everything in the reminders trash
actions.description: Empty the task trash through entity.empty_trash with kind task. Irreversible and takes no id: every task in the trash is destroyed now, as purge destroys one.

actions.name: restore-task
phrasings: bring back the plumber task
restore the task I deleted
undelete buy milk
actions.description: Bring a trashed task back through entity.restore, with the subtasks trashed with it; a subtask trashed on its own stays where it was.

actions.name: create-project
phrasings: make a project called Home renovation
create a list named Errands
start a Finance project in the Personal area
actions.description: Create a project or an area through container.create. A project may sit in an area (its `parent`), and has a color and a place in the list.

icon.description: A key of design/icons.toml a list may wear.

actions.name: rename-list
phrasings: rename the Home renovation project to House projects
call the Errands list Chores
retitle the Finance project
actions.description: Retitle a project or an area through entity.retitle.

actions.name: create-section
phrasings: add a section called Kitchen to Home renovation
create a Waiting section in Errands
add a Q4 section to Finance
actions.description: Create a section within a task project through container.create (the project is its `parent`).

actions.name: add-task-tag
phrasings: tag the plumber task as home
label buy milk errands
add the tag urgent to the taxes task
actions.description: Tag a task through tag.add: a free-form label shared with every other app that tags; minted on first use. Idempotent.

actions.name: remove-task-tag
phrasings: remove the home tag from the plumber task
untag buy milk
take the urgent label off the taxes task
actions.description: Remove one tag from a task through tag.remove; the tag survives for other things.

actions.name: star-task
phrasings: star the plumber task
flag the taxes
mark buy milk as flagged
actions.description: Star a task through flag.set: Reminders calls the starred flag Flag, and a flagged task joins the Flagged list. Idempotent.

actions.name: unstar-task
phrasings: unstar the plumber task
take the flag off the taxes
unflag buy milk
actions.description: Take the flag off a task through flag.clear. Idempotent.

actions.name: style-container
phrasings: make the Errands list blue
give the Groceries list a heart icon
change the colour of my Home list
actions.description: Set or clear the colour (one of the eight list colours) and the icon of a list through container.style. A key that is present is set (null clears it); a key that is absent is left alone.

icon.description: A key of design/icons.toml a list or calendar may wear.

actions.name: attach
phrasings: attach the receipt to the tax reminder
add the boarding pass to my packing reminder
attach the quote to the plumber reminder
actions.description: Attach or detach any file to a reminder through the shared edge verbs.

actions.name: detach
phrasings: take the receipt off the tax reminder
remove the quote from the plumber reminder
detach the boarding pass from my packing reminder
actions.description: Take an attachment off a reminder through the shared edge verbs.

actions.name: export-ics
phrasings: export my reminders as ics
save a list as a calendar file
send someone this reminder as an ics file
actions.description: Answer every list's reminders, one list's, or one reminder, as a calendar file (.ics) of to-dos through task.export_ics. Writes nothing.

actions.name: follow-reminders
phrasings: import my phone's reminders
sync reminders from this phone
pull in my reminders
actions.description: Follow the phone's Reminders through follow.reminders, one list at a time: a field the member never changed follows the phone, one they changed stands, a reminder the vault does not know is matched by title to a task of the member's own before one is added, one the phone completes completes the task, and one gone from a complete read goes to the trash if the member never edited it.

color.description: The colour the phone paints the store with, as the design wheel names it.

size.description: How large the bytes a record names are, counted by the phone; the command claims them.

actions.name: stop-following
phrasings: stop reading the phone's reminders
disconnect reminders on this phone
stop following phone reminders
actions.description: Stop following one of the phone's Reminders lists through follow.stop: its origin is retired and its tasks forget their source. Every task stays, an ordinary one from now on. It is the Undo of follow-reminders, and it asks first because following again needs the phone's own read.

queries.name: board
queries.description: The task board as a bounded window (newest open tasks by creation, caller-sized, families kept whole; the logbook read is capped at its visible 50 most recently closed), each row carrying its tags (`[{concept_id, label}]`) and what it is about, plus the distinct tag list (`[{concept_id, label}]`) seen within the window — never a whole-table pull; `truncated` is the open walk's own cursor — it exists or it does not — rather than a guess from the row count.

view.description: How the rows are grouped; the rows are the same board read whichever is asked.

queries.name: task
queries.description: One task by id, whether or not any board window holds it: the task with its subtasks, tags, project and section, and its parent when it is a subtask.

queries.name: projects
queries.description: The live projects and their sections, with open counts, in their order.

queries.name: catch-up
queries.description: What fell behind while the member was away: dated work past due, repeating work that missed occurrences, and undated work sitting too long, each as a pile.

queries.name: reminders
queries.description: The open tasks that carry a reminder and a due, nearest stored due first, in the board's row shape (a repeating task's next period read as its due): one statement over the due index, at most a caller-sized window of them, so an old task's reminder is never pushed out by newer work. A trashed task is left out; `truncated` says more exist beyond the window.

queries.name: trash
queries.description: The tasks in the 30-day trash, most recently trashed first, each with when it was deleted and when it is erased.

queries.name: smart-counts
queries.description: How many open tasks are due today, overdue and flagged, counted over every open task in the vault and never over a board's window, so the figure is true at any vault size. It counts the open top-level tasks the board draws (an unfinished subtask of a closed or trashed task counts as its own) and reads each due as the board does, in the request's zone against the vault clock. Returns three numbers and the `today_day` they were counted against; no rows.

queries.name: due-rows
queries.description: The open tasks due soonest, read in due order over every open task in the vault and never over a board's window of the newest, so the rows are the earliest at any vault size: window `now` is overdue first and then due today (each by due, then the member's order), window `timed_ahead` is the tasks with a time due today or tomorrow. At most `limit` rows (1 to 12, default 6), the open top-level tasks the board draws, each placed as the board places it (a repeating task by its next period). Rows are single tasks: no families.

queries.name: search
queries.description: Full-text search over events and tasks through the vault's one index — the ranked non-cancelled events (title, description and place) in the upcoming row shape, and the ranked tasks (title, description and project) in the board's row shape, each with a hit snippet, never a whole-table pull.

queries.name: attachments
queries.description: What is attached to one event or task, a page at a time: each attachment's id, kind (document or photo), title, media type, byte size and where its bytes are served, in the order of the attached file's id. Pass the page's `next` cursor as `after` for the next page. An id that is no live event or task answers an empty page, and an attached file in the trash is left out until it is restored.
